P-01.summary: Built V1.1 A/B/C comparison simulator. Fixed the V1.0 'noprediction' bug (was still using trend predictor for isolation). V1.1 'B_reactive' correctly isolates on actual failure (G < 10% of healthy). A/B/C comparison across 5 seeds produced three honest findings: (1) Reactive redundancy (B) is WORSE than single-path (A) — fails 35% faster because sudden isolation causes ICP spikes. (2) Predictive isolation (C) extends survival 7-9x (7.66h vs 0.84-1.29h) and reduces peak ICP by 60-70% (22 mmHg vs 37-59 mmHg). (3) C's controller energy is 4380 alpha-changes/hour — real engineering concern for battery/wear. Central buyer question answered: YES, prediction materially outperforms redundancy. But neither system meets 24h survival.

P-04.summary: Built WET_LAB_PROGRAM_SMALLEST.json: 3-phase, 8-month, $100-200K program with go/no-go gates. Phase 1: which enzyme works in CSF (30-day stability test, 3 candidates: NEP, IDE, MMP-9). Phase 2: can it remain active when immobilized (2 strategies: EDC/NHS covalent, PEG hydrogel). Phase 3: does pulsation sync improve clearance (1.3x target). Each phase has a GO/NO-GO gate — if Phase 1 fails, P-04 DIES. This is the opposite of the R276 pattern where we built documentation around an unresolved enzyme.

P-09.to: same state + molecule-selection research program defined
P-09.summary: Built MOLECULE_SELECTION_RESEARCH_PROGRAM.json: 6-step, 14-month, $200-500K program. Step 1: candidate molecular mechanisms (5 classes: molecular rotors, mechanophores, pressure-sensitive liposomes, piezoelectric-activated reservoirs, phase-change materials). Step 2: feasibility screen (computational chemistry). Step 3: transport model (CFD). Step 4: detectability (sensor assessment). Step 5: safety constraints. Step 6: shortlist + experimental plan. Each step has GO/NO-GO gate. Probability of viable molecule: 20-40%. If no molecule found, architecture dies — negative result is itself valuable.
